title: Activate your chest for the bench and keep your pectoral tendons healthy in less
summary: A quick tip for lifters who don't feel their chest when benching: do one-arm band or SPRI upward flyes between bench sets. Arm bend adjusts difficulty and biceps involvement. He does sets of 8-12 during warm-ups and burnouts between heavy sets. The work also promotes pec blood flow and tendon health by training a pattern different from horizontal presses.

claims.claim: If you are triceps- or shoulder-dominant and don't feel your chest on the bench, do upward band movements between bench sets; it helped him feel and grow his chest.
Do the band fly one arm at a time, rotating the arm inward; the more bent the arm, the more biceps it uses, the straighter the arm, the more chest and the harder it gets.
He does band chest flyes with a very bent arm because a straight arm hurts his shoulders.
With a SPRI band, step on it and do standing flyes; bending the arms more makes it easier.
Do sets of 8-12 band flyes between bench warm-up sets, and burnout sets between heavy bench sets.
He benches with a Slingshot, which takes work off the chest, so the chest has energy left for pump work between sets.
Band flyes promote blood flow to the pecs and keep pectoral tendons healthy by working a pattern different from horizontal presses.
